subject: general
question: As the object is moved from the pole towards the focus of a concave mirror, the corresponding image moves from ______ and the image is _______.

options.text: pole to infinity, virtual and erect
infinity to pole, virtual and erect
pole to Infinity, real and inverted
infinity to pole, real and inverted

solution:
The correct answer is __**pole to infinity, virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A concave mirror is a type of curved mirror where the reflective surface bulges inward.
 
• When light rays that are initially parallel to the principal axis reflect off the surface, they converge at a point known as the focal point.

Explanation__: The behavior of a concave mirror depends on the position of the object:

__
 
• Object at infinity: Produces a real image at the focal point.
 
• Object beyond the focal point: Produces a real, inverted image between the focal point and the center of curvature.
 
• Object at the focal point: No image is formed as rays reflect parallel and never meet.
 
• Object between the focal point and the mirror: Produces a virtual, upright, and magnified image behind the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a7b08f7def9b7610813baabc7d001e3e602d85e09c407eaf215cab43a85d09.png]
